name: Vinaceous-Brown
lede: Vinaceous-Brown is a greyed wine-red from Ridgway's 1912 bird-color atlas, the same measured hue our library also files under the name [[rose-brown]].

sections.title: Two names, one hue
sections.body: Ridgway's 1912 systematic nomenclature places Vinaceous-Brown on plate XXXIX, hue 5''', tone i [1]. The ISCC-NBS revision of 1955 groups the same chip as "grayish red," block 19 [1]. Our library carries a second name, [[rose-brown]], at the identical measured hex — two naming traditions landing on the same color by coincidence, not by borrowing [2]. The nearest distinct neighbor is [[monkey-skin]], a shade warmer and lighter [2]. Further out, [[cameo-brown]] and [[deep-livid-brown]] sit in the same small cluster [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a match for Vinaceous-Brown in 284 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.2 percent, more common than 67 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 39 of 1,674 paintings, 3.0 times the rate expected from that century's share of the archive [3]. Inside a painting it is usually hidden rather than prominent, by lightness rank, in 48 percent of its appearances [3]. Maurice Denis used it most: 6 of his 43 paintings here carry it, 7.5 times his peers' rate [3]. The earliest archive match dates to 1000, nine centuries before Ridgway recorded the name in 1912, which shows only a look-alike hue surviving an old photograph, not the name itself [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[3].
